evidence.claim: TreeHouse Foods completed the acquisition of Farmer Brothers' Northlake, Texas coffee facility and non-Direct Store Delivery coffee business for approximately $100 million, adding roasting, grinding, flavoring, blending, single-serve, ready-to-drink, and broader private-label coffee capabilities.

evidence.claim: TreeHouse's annual-report disclosure states that the Direct Ship coffee business and Northlake facility acquisition enables greater category depth in an end-to-end private-label coffee offering.

Westrock Coffee describes itself as an integrated coffee, tea, flavors, extracts, and ingredients solutions provider serving retail, foodservice, restaurant, convenience-store, travel-center, non-commercial, CPG, and hospitality industries.

Westrock's positioning around traceability, sustainability programs, customization, extracts, and integrated beverage solutions makes it a plausible chokepoint candidate when restaurant and foodservice customers need scale, consistency, and custom beverage innovation.

Farmer Brothers' annual-report disclosure identifies customers including restaurant, department and convenience-store chains, hotels, casinos, healthcare facilities, gourmet coffee houses, foodservice distributors, and retail/private-brand channels.

Farmer Brothers sold its Northlake facility and non-Direct Store Delivery coffee business to TreeHouse Foods, leaving the remaining thesis more dependent on DSD, key accounts, route density, equipment/service reliability, and turnaround execution.

memory_update.text: WEST is a high-relevance underfollowed candidate for B2B coffee, tea, flavors, extracts, and beverage ingredient supply, but later layers must stress-test debt, free cash flow, customer concentration, and extract/ingredient capacity utilization.
FARM is a node-pure but below-$300M speculative shadow candidate; include only with explicit micro-cap, leverage, route-density, and turnaround-risk warnings.

Need stronger primary-source verification of customer concentration and named restaurant/foodservice relationships across WEST, FARM, THS, and JVA before moving any candidate beyond Layer 1.

node: B2B coffee roasting, extracts, tea, syrups, and beverage ingredient supply
summary: Expanded the B2B coffee and beverage ingredient supply node with a two-lane universe. The reference/context lane is TreeHouse Foods, a scaled private-label food and beverage manufacturer that acquired Farmer Brothers' Northlake coffee facility and direct-ship coffee business. The underfollowed lane includes Westrock Coffee as a scaled but financially higher-risk integrated coffee, tea, flavors, extracts, and ingredients platform, plus Farmer Brothers and Coffee Holding as speculative micro-cap shadow candidates with unusually direct exposure to foodservice coffee, tea, private-label, and direct-store/service channels. This pass intentionally avoids mega-cap restaurant and coffee retailers except as customer/context anchors.
